name: Matheme — Formal Neighbours
description: Seventeen formal neighbours, each exactly worked on its own terms: ordinals, division pluralisms, Sheffer stroke, Laws of Form, Russell, Gödel, FDE, CRT, trivial ring, group completion, iterants, cross-ratio, Bloch sphere, Noether, quaternions, calculus, attractors. Source revision dbf3b17; census T25.

text.title: Von Neumann Ordinals — The Predecessors Retained
text.italic: S(n) = n ∪ {n}: each new number holds the entire preceding number.
text.body: 0 := ∅; S(n) = n ∪ {n}. Then 1 = {∅} — one member, whose member has none: |1| = 1, 0 ∈ 1, 0 ≠ 1. Enclosing alone would give {{∅}} — not two; successor retains the predecessors AND encloses the whole: n ⊆ S(n) and n ∈ S(n). So n = {0,…,n−1}, |n| = n, and m < n ⟺ m ∈ n. The linking-one reading (Argued) takes this as its exact floor: retention through determination.

text.title: Division Pluralisms — What the Denominator Permits
text.italic: Lack of a solution and lack of uniqueness are distinct obstructions.
text.body: In a field, 0x=0 for all x: no quotient for a/0 (no solution), while 0/0 fails differently (every q solves it) — distinct obstructions. Cancelling 6·0 = 17·0 would give 6=17. Bhāskara keeps a/0 written, denominator visible — khahara under its own operations; Dutta: no automatic a=0h. Totalising: ι(0)=0 gives D(6,0)=0 as the new operation's value. Projective J([a:b])=[b:a] is total — a quotient still fails at [0:0].

text.title: Sheffer Stroke — One Operation, Every Boolean Function
text.italic: Repetition earns negation; composition reaches every finite table.
text.body: p∣q := ¬(p∧q). Repetition earns negation: p∣p = ¬p; composition restores AND and OR: (p∣q)∣(p∣q), (p∣p)∣(q∣q). XOR in four gates; the row construction then reaches every finite Boolean function — functional completeness, constants included via an unused input. NOR is the dual, equally complete. The native slash keeps a different account — AND/OR retaining terms and pairings, 2+2² — and a NAND output (three pairs yield 1) cannot reconstruct its inputs.

text.title: Laws of Form and Varela — Crossing, Re-entry, Self-Indication
text.italic: The static equation has no two-valued solution; the delayed recurrence has two alternating trajectories.
text.body: Calling MM = M; crossing C(M) = U. Re-entry x = C(x) has no two-valued solution; delayed, x_{t+1} = C(x_t) alternates U, M, U, M — the delay and held state are extra dynamical structure. Varela adds an autonomous value: C(A) = A, and A·C(A) = A ≠ M — a changed arithmetic, not an average of the oscillation, and not QL zero. Ø in 0 → Ø → X → Ø/X → 1 ↷ 0/1 marks occluded ground, not the unmarked value.

text.title: Russell's Paradox and Types — Restricting the Formed Totality
text.italic: The contradiction identifies permissions that cannot all remain in force; the repairs differ.
text.body: Comprehension for x∉x gives R with R∈R ↔ R∉R — a proved contradiction. Typing blocks formation: xⁿ ∈ xⁿ needs n = n+1, so the definition is not well-formed; typed collection still constructs A¹, B², complements. Separation restricts instead: R_S ∉ S, no inconsistency — separation never promised membership in its input. Two different repairs; the account states which totality it formed and what that totality may contain.

text.title: Gödel Incompleteness — The Proof Relation Turned Inward
text.italic: Effective proof checking lets arithmetic encode its own proof relation; the fixed point obstructs completeness.
text.body: Code proofs into arithmetic: Prov_T(a) := ∃p Prf_T(p,a). The diagonal lemma gives G_T ↔ ¬Prov_T(⌜G_T⌝). If T proved G_T, the proof would have a code — contradiction; consistently, T ⊬ G_T, and G_T is true in ℕ. Rosser: two-sided unprovability from consistency alone. The derivability conditions then give T ⊢ Con(T) → G_T, so T ⊬ Con(T). Undecidable in T: T+R and T+¬R are both consistent, and the enlargement has its own fixed point.

entities.name: SILENCE at #5 — a return, not a value

text.title: FDE, Four-Valued Logic and Catuṣkoṭi
text.italic: Two independent supports, four statuses; contradiction retained without arbitrary consequence.
text.body: Two independent supports, four statuses: t, f, b = both, n = neither. Negation swaps supports; b∧n = f and b∨n = t — truth order, distinct from the information order where n is bottom, b top. Designated D = {t,b}: p, ¬p ⊬ q — contradiction without explosion; at n, p∨¬p fails. Priest's e is infectious and e ≠ n. The native crossing puts encounter first; SILENCE at #5 is a return, not a fifth value.

scenes.name: Chinese remainder, six as two by three
scenes.character: Chinese remainder, six as two by three

text.title: Chinese Remainder: Six as Two by Three
text.italic: One mod-6 address becomes two independent residues, and 3a+4b recovers it.
text.body: φ([k]₆) = ([k]₂,[k]₃) hits every pair exactly once; the inverse ψ(a,b) = 3a+4b mod 6 — (1,2) gives 11 ≡ 5. Reductions preserve + and ×: a ring isomorphism, needing gcd(2,3)=1 — with 2 and 4, (1,0) is impossible. ℤ/6 is not a field: 2·3 ≡ 0, displayed componentwise as (0,2)·(1,0) = (0,0). One address, two independent residues, lossless both ways — no QL positions assigned by algebra alone.

text.title: The One-Element Ring
text.italic: Ring axioms plus 0=1 force one element; a precise boundary for an algebraic interpretation.
text.body: Distributivity: a·0 = a·(0+0) = a·0 + a·0, so a·0 = 0. Assume 0=1: a = a·1 = a·0 = 0 for every a — one element, tables 0+0=0, 0·0=0. Consistent under the stated convention; not itself a contradiction, though it violates any added nontriviality requirement. No field element satisfies 0·b=1. The native 0/1 = 1/0 concerns orientations of one relation, not ring identities — the collapse is a boundary, not a refutation.

scenes.name: group completion and conditions of loss
scenes.character: group completion and conditions of loss

text.title: Group Completion and the Conditions of Loss
text.italic: Injectivity is equivalent to cancellation: completion loses nothing for ℕ and everything for {0,e}.
text.body: Pairs (a,b) = a−b, with a stabiliser t in (a,b)~(c,d) iff a+d+t = c+b+t; classes form G(M), i(a) = [(a,0)] universal. The criterion: i injective ⟺ M cancellative. ℕ completes to ℤ injectively — nothing is lost. But {0, e} with e+e=e forces i(e) = 0 in any group: the completion is trivial, two elements become one. Whether an accounting suppresses essential distinctions depends on the actual field and map — not a theorem about subtraction.

text.title: Kauffman Iterants
text.italic: i = ση: the square is negative because the sign pattern and the shift anticommute.
text.body: An alternation read as [a,b] or [b,a]; the shift η with η²=1 and [a,b]η = η[b,a] carries phase through products. With ε = [−1,1], i = εη: ηε = −εη, so i² = [−1,−1] = −1 — neither factor alone, their ordered composite. J = [[0,−1],[1,0]], J² = −I; aI+bJ ≅ ℂ. R(x) = −1/x has the orbit 1, −1, 1, … and no fixed point; the algebra enlarges so a fixed point can be expressed. A representation need not recover every process expression.

text.title: Cross-Ratio under Fractional-Linear Transformation
text.italic: A quantity that survives a specified transformation — and is exact about where it fails.
text.body: λ = ((z₁−z₃)(z₂−z₄))/((z₁−z₄)(z₂−z₃)), convention explicit. For f(z) = (az+b)/(cz+d), Δ = ad−bc ≠ 0, differences pick up cancelling factors: λ is invariant. (0,1,2,3) gives 4/3; z+5 keeps it; swapping two inputs gives 3/4 — order matters. Squaring the inputs gives 32/27: outside the class, distinctness survives while the invariant fails. The native (0/1)/(1/0) keeps its own seam — resemblance of nested fractions is not a map.

text.title: A Pure Qubit and the Bloch Sphere
text.italic: A formal neighbour, exactly worked: the sphere of pure states, the ball of mixtures.
text.body: Rays α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ up to phase: ℂP¹, parametrised cos(θ/2)|0⟩ + e^{iφ}sin(θ/2)|1⟩ with Bloch vector r of length 1 — pure states on the sphere, mixtures inside, eigenvalues (1±|r|)/2. |+⟩ and |−⟩ share probabilities 1/2, 1/2 and differ by relative phase: r = ±(1,0,0). Antipodal r are orthogonal rays; ±ψ are the same ray — two "opposites" not to be fused. A formal neighbour, not the origin of the core's ontology.

entities.name: the drive breaks energy, not rotation

text.title: Noether: Symmetry and Conservation
text.italic: Name what transforms, prove what is preserved, distinguish a change of representative from a change of law.
text.body: δℒ = E_a·δφ^a + ∂_μ(π_a^μ·δφ^a): for a constant-parameter symmetry with boundary term, j = π·Δ − B and ∂j = −E·Δ — on solutions, conserved. The oscillator: rotation gives ℓ = m(xẏ − yẋ), ℓ̇ = 0; time translation gives H, conserved when L_t = 0. With k(t), ℓ̇ = 0 still and Ḣ ≠ 0 — the drive transfers energy. Arbitrary-function symmetries give identities, not charges. Only observable-preserving changes are gauge candidates.

text.title: Quaternion Q8 and Rotation
text.italic: ij = k but ji = −k: order matters; q and −q give the same rotation.
text.body: i² = j² = k² = ijk = −1; ij = k but ji = −k — order matters. The six signed imaginary units alone are not a subgroup: i·i = −1 lies outside; adjoining ±1 gives Q8. Rotation: v ↦ qvq⁻¹ with q = cos(θ/2) + u·sin(θ/2) turns by θ about u; q and −q agree, so SU(2) → SO(3) is 2:1 — a continuous double cover, distinct from the Klein orientation cover and the torus's infinite cover. Q8 ≠ the eight determinations by cardinality.

scenes.character: calculus: local rate, constant of return

entities.name: the constant is the only freedom

text.title: Calculus: Local Rate and the Constant of Return
text.italic: Differentiation retains rate and discards an additive level; the condition that selects a member is new data.
text.body: F′ = 2x has the family x² + C: same slope 2 at x=1, different values — differentiation keeps rate, drops level. The mean value theorem: H′ = 0 on one interval forces H constant — the constant is the only freedom (on disconnected domains, one per component). F(1) = 4 selects C = 3: new data, not contained in the derivative. The definite integral cancels the constant — a different question. ∞/dx keeps its eightfold office beside this exact neighbour.

text.title: Attractors, Basins and a Bifurcation
text.italic: x′ = μx − x³: the equilibrium structure changes at μ=0; boundary sensitivity is not chaos.
text.body: x′ = μx − x³, the negative gradient of x⁴/4 − μx²/2. μ<0: one attractor at 0. μ>0: 0 unstable, ±√μ attracting — a supercritical pitchfork at μ=0, where −x³ still attracts. For μ=1, +ε and −ε diverge to opposite basins: boundary sensitivity, not strange-attractor chaos — the destinations are simple equilibria. A trajectory is read within the changed field, not as a novel instance of an unchanged rule.
